Hi Samir — great to chat earlier. Quick recap and two small asks so we can get a pricing sketch over to procurement.

1) Summary of what you told us (confirm if I missed anything):
- Use case: assisted coding for clinical documentation + automated summarization of patient encounter notes.
- Integration: on top of Brightwell’s ETL; calls will include both free-text prompts and structured fields.
- SLA target: 95th pctile latency < 350ms for interactive flows; batch summarization can be async.

2) Sizing asks (what we need from you to finalize a target price / commitment):
- Typical prompt length (avg prompt tokens): please confirm avg tokens sent in request (prompt).
- Typical completion length (avg completion tokens): average generated length, and peak length when summaries are longer.
- Context depth needs: what percent of requests require extended context (32k/128k) vs standard 8k?
- Monthly volume envelope: best-guess monthly generation tokens and any seasonal peaks.
- Budget range: ballpark monthly budget and any target $/1M tokens you have in mind.

To make it easy, if you can reply with numbers for the five bullets above I’ll build 2 pricing scenarios (hosted + reserved commitment) and include an option for 32k/128k context add-ons. Attached a quick template we can fill (redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx).

Next step: once we have numbers, I’ll share a one-page MAP and proposed trial terms (1–2 week pilot + 30-day performance review).

Thanks — appreciate the time.

—Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers we can share now (engineering will follow up with logs/export next week for exact token counts).

- Avg prompt tokens: ~180 tokens (typical structured + free-text prompt).
- Avg completion tokens: ~720 tokens (most summaries are 2–4 short paragraphs).
- Context depth: ~95% of requests fit in 8k. ~4% need 32k context (they pull in recent chart notes + attachments). ~<0.5% would need 128k (rare, multi-visit longitudinal pulls for research).
- Monthly tokens (generation only): ~120 million tokens/month (we count completions + prompts). Peaks in Q4 ~20% higher.
- Embeddings: about 1.5M embeddings/month (for search/recall).
- Budget: our procurement range for pilot/initial rollout is $12k–$20k/month. For long term we are looking for target pricing in the ballpark of $18–$22 per 1M generated tokens (we understand embeddings/different SKU may be separate).

Happy to share logs; procurement asked for an initial pricing sketch to evaluate whether this fits their current budget range.

Thanks — Samir

Samir / Procurement — thanks again for the numbers. Per our internal alignment I’ve sketched two concise options below to fit the $12k–$20k/mo procurement envelope while giving Brightwell predictable economics.

Quick notes on assumptions used:
- We calculated generated tokens = prompts + completions (your 120M/month).
- Blended tail: priced a blended context uplift to account for 4% 32k and 0.5% 128k usage (small premium applied to those requests).
- Embeddings billed separately at $0.80 per 1k embeddings (we can adjust if you want embeddings in a capped package).

Option A — Pilot (low commitment)
- Duration: 30-day pilot; up to 15M gen tokens included.
- Price: $40 per 1M tokens for pilot usage above included 15M (hosted list).
- 32k requests: +20% per-token uplift on those requests. 128k: +50% uplift.
- Trial support: access to SEs for integration + 1 performance review.
- Goal: validate latency & quality, instrument exact token usage for a committed offer.

Option B — Initial commitment (preferred for budget predictability)
- Term: 12 months; committed 120M gen tokens/month.
- Effective blended price: $19 per 1M generated tokens (blended across normal + 32k/128k tail).
- Overage: $22 per 1M tokens above commitment.
- Embeddings: $0.65 per 1k (volume discount).
- 32k-capable model included for no extra infra fee; 128k requests incur a 40% per-token premium due to memory footprint.
- Additional: 10% discount on seeding Dedicated pool if Brightwell opts for Dedicated after month 3.

Rationale: Option B aims to land inside your stated $18–$22 target while giving us predictability to optimize batching/caching for your workload. Option A preserves flexibility but is more expensive per token.
